title: mcp: run_action refuses every action on a sys_* object, so an agent cannot reach the identity actions (ban_user, impersonate_user, set_user_password) that REST POST /actions serves
body:
domain:server#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgXcN9HaZYSEUdJWEjw

Filing gate: ② a gap against a stated design goal, found in the contract review of #27649 (card #27506, ruling C step 2) and carried by the dev's os-dev-report as out of scope, class b. Read on the tree, not measured over HTTP.
reach: `objectstack-ai/objectstack` main `144702ca5d`. MCP `run_action` has two `sys_*` refusals in front of the same action-execution path that `POST /api/v1/actions/:object/:action` serves:
- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` (`run_action` handler, around line 1294): refuses when `objectName` is a `sys_*` name, unless the tool registration passed `allowSystemObjects: true` (`RegisterActionToolsOptions`, around line 275; default false).
- `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` `invokeBusinessAction` (around line 2686): `isSystemObjectName(objectName)` throws `Action '…' is on a system object and is not exposed via MCP`. This one is **unconditional**: no option lifts it, so `allowSystemObjects` on the MCP side cannot open it either.

Business reason: the maintainer's stated goal (ruling on #27506, 2026-10-29) is that agents and humans use one system. After #27649 the REST action door serves the packaged identity actions on `sys_user` (`ban_user`, `unban_user`, `set_user_password`, `impersonate_user`, …) to a caller who holds the action's permissions, behind the packaged-action switch. An agent over MCP is refused every one of them by object name before any of those gates is consulted, so the ruling's "exposes them to agents with no further change" does not hold for MCP.
Reader who acts: the triage seat. This is a posture choice, not a mechanical fix: the `sys_*` refusal is a deliberate fail-closed default (`mcp-http-tools.ts` header comment, line 28). Whether, and under which gate (the per-action AI-exposure flag that `invokeBusinessAction` already checks for ADR-0011, an explicit allow-list, or the existing `allowSystemObjects` option made to reach the runtime guard), is likely a `needs_decision` for the maintainer.
Dedupe: scanned every open issue title for `run_action`, `MCP` and `mcp`. Hits: #27429, #27402, #27401, #27293, #26702, #25583 and #20791. None is about `sys_*` action exposure.

Back-link: #27506 · #27649

⛔ Not a claim. Grading is triage's.

## Symptom

An MCP client that calls `run_action` with `objectName: "sys_user"` and an identity action gets a refusal naming the system object. The same caller, with the same credentials, can invoke the action through `POST /api/v1/actions/sys_user/<action>` once #27649 lands.

## Expected

To be decided. One system for agents and humans suggests that MCP `run_action` reaches a `sys_*` action under the same gates as the REST door: the packaged-action switch, the action's permissions, the ADR-0011 AI-exposure flag, and the destructive-confirmation member. It should not hit a blanket object-name refusal. Keeping the blanket refusal is also a valid outcome if it is written down as deliberate, with the REST door named as the agent's path.

## Mechanism

Two guards, listed above. The runtime guard runs before `isHeadlessInvokableAction` and before `actionAiExposureError`, so no per-action declaration can open it. The dogfood case for #27649's MCP arm runs on a non-`sys_*` object for this reason.
